nodes.title: Bounded partial quotients for a cubic of Ayadi et al

nodes.summary: Let $p \in \mathbb{F}_2[x]$ have degree at least $1$. If $f \in \mathbb{F}_2((x^{-1}))$ satisfies $f^3 + p^{-1} f + 1 = 0$, then $f$ has bounded partial quotients.
nodes.title: Baum–Sweet: cubics with bounded partial quotients

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 0$ and let $P, Q \in \mathbb{F}_2[x]$ with $P + Q^{2^n} \ne 0$ and $P + Q^{2^n} \ne 1$. Then some $f \in \mathbb{F}_2((x^{-1}))$ satisfies $f^{2^n+1} + Q f^{2^n} + P f + QP + 1 = 0$ and has partial quotients $b_0 = Q$ and $b_k = P^{2^{(k-1)n}} + Q^{2^{kn}}$ for all $k \ge 1$, that is, $f = [Q; P + Q^{2^n}, P^{2^n} + Q^{2^{2n}}, P^{2^{2n}} + Q^{2^{3n}}, \dots]$.
nodes.title: Baum–Sweet: explicit continued fractions of roots

nodes.summary: Let $n > 1$ and let $g \in \mathbb{F}_2[x]$ have degree at least $1$. If $f \in \mathbb{F}_2((x^{-1}))$ satisfies $f^{2^n+1} + g^{-1} f + 1 = 0$, then $f$ does not have bounded partial quotients.
nodes.title: Baum–Sweet: unbounded partial quotients for higher degrees

nodes.summary: If $\alpha \in \mathbb{F}_2((x^{-1}))$ satisfies $x\alpha^3 + \alpha + x = 0$, then every partial quotient $b_n$ of $\alpha$, $n \ge 0$, has degree at most $2$ in $x$.
nodes.title: Baum–Sweet cubic: partial quotients of degree at most 2

nodes.title: Small roots of a hyperquadratic equation have unbounded partial quotients

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$. The complete quotients of the continued fraction expansion of $\alpha$ are $\alpha_0 = \alpha$ and $\alpha_{n+1} = (\alpha_n - [\alpha_n])^{-1}$ for $n \ge 0$, where $[\beta]$ is the polynomial part of $\beta$ and $0^{-1} = 0$. So the complete quotients become $0$ after a finite expansion ends.
nodes.title: Complete quotients of a Laurent series

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, let $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ and let $b_0, b_1, \dots$ be its partial quotients. The denominators of the convergents of $\alpha$ are given by $Q_{-1} = 0$, $Q_0 = 1$ and $Q_{n+1} = b_{n+1} Q_n + Q_{n-1}$ for $n \ge 0$. They are indexed from $0$ here: the $k$-th term of the sequence is $Q_{k-1}$.
nodes.title: Denominators of the convergents

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and let $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ have partial quotients $b_0, b_1, \dots$. The numerators of the convergents of $\alpha$ are $P_{-1} = 1$, $P_0 = b_0$ and $P_{n+1} = b_{n+1} P_n + P_{n-1}$ for $n \ge 0$. The sequence is indexed with a shift of one: its term at $n \ge 0$ is $P_{n-1}$.
nodes.title: Numerators of the convergents of a Laurent series

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and let $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ have partial quotients $b_0, b_1, \dots$. Let $P_n$ and $Q_n$ be the numerators and denominators of its convergents, given by $P_{-1} = 1$, $Q_{-1} = 0$, $P_0 = b_0$, $Q_0 = 1$, $P_{n+1} = b_{n+1} P_n + P_{n-1}$ and $Q_{n+1} = b_{n+1} Q_n + Q_{n-1}$. Then $P_1 = b_1 b_0 + 1$ and $Q_1 = b_1$.
nodes.title: The convergent $P_1 / Q_1$ of a Laurent series

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and let $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ be irrational, with partial quotients $b_0, b_1, \dots$ and convergents $P_n / Q_n$, where $P_{-1} = 1$, $Q_{-1} = 0$, $P_0 = b_0$, $Q_0 = 1$, $P_{n+1} = b_{n+1} P_n + P_{n-1}$ and $Q_{n+1} = b_{n+1} Q_n + Q_{n-1}$. nodes.title: Close rational approximations and convergents

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field. A Laurent series $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ with partial quotients $b_0, b_1, \dots$ has bounded partial quotients if there is an integer $B$ such that for every $n \ge 0$ and every integer $k > B$ the coefficient of $x^k$ in $b_n$ is zero, that is, every nonzero $b_n$ is a polynomial in $x$ of degree at most $B$.
nodes.title: Laurent series with bounded partial quotients

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field. In $K((x^{-1}))$, the product of the variable $x$ and the series $x^{-1}$ (coefficient $1$ at $x^{-1}$ and $0$ elsewhere) is $1$.
nodes.title: The variable $x$ times $x^{-1}$ is one

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field. Formal Laurent series in $x^{-1}$ over $K$ are realized as Laurent series $\sum_n c_n X^n$ in $X = x^{-1}$, and the variable $x$ is the series $X^{-1}$, with coefficient $1$ at $X^{-1}$ and $0$ elsewhere.
nodes.title: The variable $x$ of $K((x^{-1}))$

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field. A Laurent series $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ is irrational if $Q \alpha \ne P$ for all polynomials $P, Q \in K[x]$ with $Q \ne 0$, where polynomials are embedded in $K((x^{-1}))$ by sending $x$ to the variable $x$.
nodes.title: Irrational Laurent series

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a finite field with $q$ elements, let $A, B, C, D \in K[x]$ with $\Delta = AD - BC \ne 0$ and $C \ne 0$, and let $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ be irrational with $\alpha = (A \alpha^q + B) / (C \alpha^q + D)$. Let $b_0, b_1, \dots$ be the partial quotients of $\alpha$ and $P_n / Q_n$ its convergents, where $P_{-1} = 1$, $Q_{-1} = 0$, $P_0 = b_0$, $Q_0 = 1$, $P_{n+1} = b_{n+1} P_n + P_{n-1}$ and…

nodes.title: Difference identities for a Möbius–Frobenius fixed point

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a finite field with $q$ elements and let $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$, with partial quotients $b_0, b_1, \dots$ and convergent numerators and denominators $P_n, Q_n$, where $P_{-1} = 1$ and $Q_{-1} = 0$. Then for every $n \ge 0$ the $n$-th partial quotient of $\alpha^q$ is $b_n^q$, and for every $n \ge -1$ the convergent numerator and denominator of $\alpha^q$ of index $n$ are $P_n^q$ and $Q_n^q$.
nodes.title: Frobenius acts on continued fractions of Laurent series

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$. The partial quotient $b_0$ of $\alpha$ is its polynomial part $[\alpha]$, and the complete quotient $\alpha_1$ is $(\alpha - [\alpha])^{-1}$, where $0^{-1} = 0$.
nodes.title: First step of the continued fraction of a Laurent series

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ and $n \ge 0$. The $n$-th partial quotient of $\alpha$ is $b_n = [\alpha_n]$, the polynomial part of the $n$-th complete quotient $\alpha_n$ of $\alpha$.
nodes.title: Partial quotients of a Laurent series

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and write $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ as $\alpha = \sum_n c_n x^{-n}$. For every integer $n$, the coefficient of $x^{-n}$ in the polynomial part $[\alpha]$ is $c_n$ if $n \le 0$ and $0$ if $n > 0$.
nodes.title: Coefficients of the polynomial part of a Laurent series

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field. In $K((x^{-1}))$ the polynomial part of $x$ is $x$, and the polynomial part of $x^{-1}$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Polynomial parts of the variable and its inverse

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and write a Laurent series $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ as $\alpha = \sum_n c_n x^{-n}$. Its polynomial part is $[\alpha] = \sum_{n \le 0} c_n x^{-n}$, the sum of the terms in nonnegative powers of $x$.
nodes.title: Polynomial part of a Laurent series

nodes.title: Distance from an irrational Laurent series to its convergents

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field. For every polynomial $P \in K[x]$, the image of $P$ in $K((x^{-1}))$ is not irrational.
nodes.title: Polynomials are not irrational

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field. The embedding $K[x] \to K((x^{-1}))$ sends the polynomial $x$ to the element $x$ of $K((x^{-1}))$.
nodes.title: The polynomial variable embeds as the Laurent variable

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field. The embedding $K[x] \to K((x^{-1}))$ is the $K$-algebra homomorphism that sends $x$ to the element $x$ of $K((x^{-1}))$, that is, it evaluates a polynomial at $x$.
nodes.title: Polynomials as Laurent series in the inverse variable

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
